title: Activation checklist UX explorations (Console) — placement + behavior + help states
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Activation checklist UX explorations (Console)
Placement options + component behavior + contextual help states
Owner: Kenji / Design
Primary partner: Marissa (Console PM)

Slide 2 — Why this exists / sprint context
Problem: Many self-serve dev signups stall before “first successful production-like inference call.”
Goal of checklist: reduce cognitive load and route users to the shortest path to success (key → first request → streaming → see latency/cost).
This deck explores UI patterns before we lock v1 scope.
Constraints:
- Must be feature-flagged + experimentable (holdouts, variants)
- Must not degrade console performance (render + data fetch)
- Copy must stay developer-first and avoid over-promising

Slide 3 — Working definition: “Activation checklist”
A small, persistent component that:
- Shows 3–5 steps toward first success
- Automatically checks steps off using events/state
- Offers contextual help when users are blocked
Non-goals:
- Full onboarding tour
- Long-form documentation (we link out)
- Complex branching flows per use case (chat vs embeddings) in v1

Slide 4 — Proposed v1 steps (for discussion)
Option A (general-purpose, minimal):
1) Create API key
2) Make your first request (2xx)
3) Try streaming
4) View latency + cost dashboard
Option B (shorter, “just ship”):
1) Create API key
2) Copy-paste a curl + get 2xx
3) View usage/cost
Notes:
- Step ordering matters (streaming as “nice to have” vs core activation)
- Dashboard view step is an early retention nudge (teaches the “why Redwood”)

Slide 5 — Placement exploration matrix
We want high visibility without feeling like an ad.
Candidate placements:
1) Dashboard home (top of content column)
2) Project overview page (right rail)
3) Project setup page (inline in setup flow)
4) Sticky widget across console (bottom-right)
Heuristics:
- Must appear within first session for new signups
- Must not obscure primary actions
- Must remain discoverable for returning users who skipped onboarding

Slide 6 — Placement option 1: Dashboard home (recommended baseline)
Pros:
- First landing surface for many users
- Allows us to pair with “Getting started” content and metrics cards
- Keeps checklist near “View latency/cost” step
Cons:
- Returning users may ignore dashboard modules
- Dashboard can be busy; risk of banner fatigue
Design notes:
- Show as compact card with progress bar
- If user completes all steps: collapse into “Completed” state with a subtle check + hide affordance

Slide 7 — Placement option 2: Project overview (right rail)
Pros:
- Contextual to “I’m in a project; now what?”
- Leaves main content for core actions
Cons:
- Right rail on smaller screens becomes a scroll trap
- Some users never visit overview; they go straight to API keys or docs
Design notes:
- Right rail card with step list
- On mobile: convert to full-width module below page header

Slide 8 — Placement option 3: Project setup page (inline)
Pros:
- Most “honest” placement: right where tasks are performed
- Can transition into a linear setup flow
Cons:
- Requires ensuring setup page is discoverable in IA
- Feels redundant if we also have inline setup content
Design notes:
- Checklist becomes a left-side stepper component (setup wizard-lite)
- Potentially increases engineering scope; consider as v2

Slide 9 — Placement option 4: Sticky widget (bottom-right)
Pros:
- Always available; good for returning/lapsed users
- Can gently animate when user completes a step
Cons:
- Higher annoyance risk / can conflict with support chat / privacy widgets
- Accessibility complexity (focus management)
Design notes:
- Default minimized; expands on click
- Consider only as variant B if dashboard module underperforms

Slide 10 — Component behavior: states + persistence
State model:
- Hidden (holdout / suppressed)
- Visible (not started)
- In progress (some steps done)
- Completed (all steps done)
Persistence rules:
- Persist completion per workspace+project (not per browser)
- “Dismiss” should be a soft-dismiss: hide for 7 days OR until user triggers a “stuck” condition
- Completed state should auto-collapse after 24h but remain accessible via “Getting started” link

Slide 11 — Step interactions (what happens on click)
Step rows should be clickable with clear CTAs:
- Create API key → deep link to API keys page + highlight “Create key” button
- Make first request → open code snippet modal (curl + SDK tabs) + copy button
- Try streaming → link to streaming example + enable streaming toggle if applicable
- View latency/cost → deep link to dashboards (filtered to project + last 24h)
Guidance:
- Prefer “do it now” actions over sending to docs
- If we link out, open in new tab and keep checklist visible

Slide 12 — Contextual help: patterns we can support
We need “help states” that are lightweight but effective.
Pattern 1: Inline helper text under a step (1–2 lines + link)
Pattern 2: Tooltip on error conditions (non-blocking)
Pattern 3: Side panel (“Need help?”) with troubleshooting + contact support
Pattern 4: Code snippet modal with error-aware tips (e.g., invalid key)
Recommendation for v1: Pattern 1 + Pattern 4 (lowest complexity, highest leverage)

Slide 13 — Contextual help examples (API key step)
Condition: user visited API keys page but didn’t create one within 60s
Help state copy (draft):
- “API keys are used to authenticate requests. Create one to get your first response in minutes.”
- Link: “Where do I put this key?” → opens snippet modal with env var examples
Edge case: org/workspace permissions
- If user lacks permission: show “Ask an admin to grant API key access” + link to invite/admin docs

Slide 14 — Contextual help examples (first request step)
Condition: user has >=2 request errors OR 401/403 within first session
Help state content (draft):
- “Seeing auth errors? Double-check you’re using the Project API key and that it’s in the Authorization header.”
- “Common fixes” accordion:
  - Missing Bearer prefix
  - Using workspace key in project route (if applicable)
  - Wrong base URL / region
CTA: “Open troubleshooting” (snippet modal + short checklist)
Support link: “Contact Support” (track clicks as guardrail signal)

Slide 15 — Contextual help examples (streaming step)
Condition: first non-stream request succeeded, but no streaming success after 24h
Help state copy (draft):
- “Streaming helps reduce time-to-first-token for chat-style UX.”
- “Try streaming example” → opens snippet modal with SDK tabs
If websocket/connection errors detected:
- “If you’re behind a corporate proxy, streaming may require allowlisting.” (link)
Note: avoid fear-mongering; keep optional

Slide 16 — Visual hierarchy + copy tone notes
Checklist should not read like marketing; it should read like a dev task list.
Copy principles:
- Short verbs (“Create”, “Send”, “Stream”, “View”)
- Avoid superlatives and unsubstantiated claims
- Prefer concrete outcomes (“Get a 2xx response”) over vague (“Start building”)
UI principles:
- Keep to one column, minimal iconography
- Show progress (e.g., 2/4 complete)
- Completion state should feel satisfying but subtle

Slide 17 — Accessibility + localization considerations (early)
Accessibility:
- Must be keyboard navigable; step rows as buttons/links with correct roles
- Visible focus ring + no hover-only affordances
- Announce progress changes via aria-live (optional; avoid chatty)
Localization:
- Step labels should be short to avoid wrapping
- Avoid embedding code tokens in translated strings where possible
- Prepare for text expansion (German/Japanese)

Slide 18 — Instrumentation hooks (for PM/Eng alignment)
Events we likely need (names illustrative; final in taxonomy):
- checklist_viewed (props: placement, variant, project_id)
- checklist_step_clicked (props: step_id)
- checklist_dismissed (props: reason=user_dismiss)
- checklist_help_opened (props: step_id, help_type)
Also rely on canonical activation events:
- api_key_created
- first_request_success (2xx)
- first_streaming_success
- dashboard_viewed (latency/cost)
Notes:
- Checklist should not require new backend endpoints if we can derive state from existing events
- Beware double-firing “viewed” events on re-render

Slide 19 — Experiment variants we can run cheaply
Variant A: Placement = dashboard module (control)
Variant B: Placement = project overview right rail
Variant C: Steps = 4-step (includes streaming + dashboard)
Variant D: Steps = 3-step (no streaming)
Guardrails:
- Increased support link clicks
- Increased error banner clicks
- Perf: no measurable slowdown on dashboard load

Slide 20 — Open questions / decisions needed this week
1) What is the primary “activation” milestone for this checklist to optimize toward? (first 2xx vs streaming success)
2) Do we treat “View latency/cost” as a step or as a post-activation nudge?
3) Where should dismissal live (per project vs per user vs per workspace)?
4) Do we need different step sets for embeddings-heavy users vs chat users (or is that v2)?
5) What is the single best default placement if we can only ship one in v1?

Slide 21 — Proposed recommendation (designer POV)
Ship v1 as:
- Placement: Dashboard home module
- Steps: 4-step (key → first request → streaming → dashboard)
- Help: inline helper text + snippet modal w/ troubleshooting
- Dismiss: “hide for 7 days” with easy re-open under “Getting started”
Reasoning: lowest scope, highest visibility, pairs well with retention nudge (dashboard)

Slide 22 — Appendix: rough copy (not final)
Header: “Finish setup”
Subhead: “Complete these steps to get your first response and see performance.”
Step labels:
- “Create an API key”
- “Send your first request (2xx)”
- “Try streaming”
- “View latency & cost”
Completion state:
- “You’re set. Want to go further?” → links: “Create a route” / “Invite teammates” / “See evals (soon)”

Notes to self (Kenji):
- Align step names with event taxonomy EXACT strings once Logan confirms
- Check if Console already has a right-rail pattern we can reuse (Alicia may know)
- Ask Leila about QA edge cases: timezones, multiple tabs, event delays
